input.quote: 9.1 Accounting. Each Party will maintain materially complete and accurate accounting records related to this Agreement in accordance with GAAP. Each Party will retain such records for [***] after the earlier of expiration or early termination of this Agreement.
input.rationale: SFJ has no audit, inspection or verification right against PB, so there is nothing for this rule to constrain. Article 9 (Records) imposes only mutual record-keeping/retention obligations on "Each Party" and grants neither Party a right to inspect or audit the other's books. The only "Audits" provision, Section 3.6, is each Party auditing the facilities of its own Permitted Third Parties (3.6.1) and PB auditing its own manufacturing facilities (3.6.2), with report copies shared — that is self-audit and reporting, not an SFJ audit of PB. Section 3.5.5 is reciprocal source-data verification of clinical records each Party is itself responsible for. Article 3.18.2 requires PB to deliver financial statements and hold periodic executive review meetings, but confers no examination right, no on-site inspection and no access to PB systems; Articles 4, 6 and 7 contain no cost- or payment-verification audit. There is no unannounced or unlimited audit right and no remote/system access language anywhere in the document, so nothing approaches walk-away territory. Because the absence of any audit right binding us is more favourable than the preferred position, we do not propose inserting frequency, notice or cost-allocation limits (or an audit right) — doing so would create a right against our client that SFJ does not currently have. Noted for the file only: if SFJ later seeks a records-audit right (e.g., over Development Costs or Approval Payments), we should condition it on once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, SFJ's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no access to PB systems.
